title: The drama you'd star in
sub: Pick a genre, give a name. Twelve scenes later, a poster.
disclaimer: Just for fun. Twelve scenes can't tell you who someone is.
name_hint: A few of the scenes call you by it, and it goes in the title.
premise: Pick a genre and you're in that world. Over twelve scenes people will say your name, and how you answer decides how the next act opens.

chaebol.label: Chaebol Romance
chaebol.tagline: The chairman, the office, the envelope

makjang.label: Makjang
makjang.tagline: Secret births, amnesia, a slap with kimchi

intern.title: First day. Your 사수 walks you round the team. “This is {name}, starting with us today.”

options.stare: You're being introduced, and you're looking at the one from the corridor
options.brief: A short bow. You answer what you're asked and nothing more
options.learn: You meet each pair of eyes and say the name back
options.mutter: “Looking forward to it.” And under your breath, “help.”

elevator.title: Of all the lifts, this one — with the person you've been avoiding. Twelve floors to go.

options.mirror: You watch the floor numbers. In the mirror, they're watching you
options.hold: Their hands are full, so you hold the door without saying anything
options.joke: “If this thing stops, we're on the news, right?”

rumour.title: The office group chat has already decided. “{name} and them — there's something going on, right?”

options.silence: You read it and don't reply. Next day nobody brings it up
options.offer: You go to them first. “If this bothers you, I'll put a stop to it”
options.rename: You say nothing and quietly rename the chat

overnight.title: Ten at night, and it's just the two of you left. “{name}, still here?”

options.stay2: You keep your eyes on the monitor and say you've got a while yet
options.coffee2: You make two coffees. You don't ask first
options.blanket: The aircon's brutal, so you drape your jacket over them
options.playlist: You put the speaker on. You have a playlist for this

hoesik.title: Round two of the 회식. The 부장 puts a microphone in your hand. “{name}, one song.”

options.ballad: You queue a ballad and don't look at one particular person
options.stand: You stand up and take the mic. The singing is a separate problem
options.swap: You put the 부장's own favourite in instead
options.tambourine: You pick up the tambourine. You do not sing

sickday.title: They're off sick. In the group chat: “{name}, could you look in on them if you've got time?”

options.porridge2: You leave the porridge at the door. You don't ring the bell
options.doctor: You take them to the clinic and sign them in yourself
options.text2: “Have you taken it?” Every two hours
options.soup: You turn up with a whole pot of chicken soup

talent.title: The company workshop talent show. Of course {name} and them are in the same group.

options.duet: You pick a duet. You don't explain
options.mc: You volunteer to host. The stage is entirely yours
options.backup: You stand behind them and hold the whole thing up
options.costume: You turn up with matching costumes nobody asked for

rooftop.title: The roof. They're up there alone, and they've clearly been crying.

options.beside: You go and stand next to them, in a way that says you're not leaving
options.coffee: You go back down, then come up again and leave a coffee
options.tissue: You hand them a tissue. “Take your time”
options.weather: “Windy up here.” You start somewhere else

rival.title: The building owner's son has noticed them. Neither the car nor the man is from around here.

options.overtime: You say nothing. You stay late with them instead
options.between: “And you are?” You end up standing between them
options.defer: If they're happy, you decide that's the right answer
options.photo: You photograph the car and post it to the group chat

mother.title: Their mother asks to meet. She sits down and slides an envelope across. “So you're {name}.”

options.refuse: You leave the envelope where it is. “I'm not taking that”
options.return: You push it back and hear her out, politely, to the end
options.listen: You start with “I know you're worried”
options.open: You open it and ask what exactly it's for

chairman.title: You're called to the chairman's office. “So you're this {name} I keep hearing about.”

options.state: “I am. And anything about them, you can say to me.”
options.bow: You bow and wait for him to speak first
options.praise: When their name comes up, you only say good things
options.deal: You ask what the terms are before he does

quitting.title: They've handed in their notice. “I wanted {name} to hear it from me.”

options.follow2: “Where to? Should I hand mine in as well.”
options.reason: You hear the whole reason out before you say anything
options.hold2: You take the letter and put it back in the drawer
options.joke2: “I'll organise the leaving do,” you say, laughing

leak.title: The company messenger has been leaked. Every message between {name} and them.

options.own: “Yes, I sent that,” you say, on the record
options.delete: You go straight to IT and get hold of the original
options.check: You go to them first. “Are you okay?”
options.screenshot: You screenshot the funniest bit and post it yourself

hospital.title: Two in the morning, a hospital corridor. Nobody has told you anything.

options.wait: You sit at the end of the corridor and wait for morning
options.family: You go to the nurses' station and say you're family
options.porridge: You go down to the shop for porridge and a blanket
options.talk: You've been talking to the person in the next chair for an hour

contract.title: “{name}. Three months. Could you pretend we're together?”

options.terms: You ask to write it down. Term, scope, how it ends
options.why: You ask why first. How bad is it
options.rings: “Sure.” Next day you turn up with matching rings

snow.title: First snow. You both remember saying you'd meet when it came.

options.go: You just go to the place. You don't message
options.snowman: You build the snowman first and send the photo

board.title: The board meeting. Your name is on the last line of the agenda.

options.omit: Your turn comes and you still don't bring them into it
options.speak: You put your hand up and go first
options.credit: You put all of it down to the team
options.walk: You close the folder and leave

airport.title: Word comes that they're at the airport. Two hours.

options.drive: You drive. You don't call until you're there
options.ring: You call first. “Stay exactly where you are.”
options.letter: You write a letter and leave it at the desk
options.gate: You get to the gate before them and wait

press.title: A story runs saying the two of you are getting married. With photos.

options.quiet: You say nothing. You don't deny it either
options.deny: You put out an official denial
options.shield: You get in front of whatever lands on them
options.frame: You frame the article and put it on your desk

wrist.title: In front of everyone, they take you by the wrist.

options.follow: You don't pull away. You go with them
options.greet: You free your hand and say hello to the room first
options.regrip: You change the grip. Hand, not wrist

ramyeon.title: Late, outside their building. “{name}, want to come up for ramyeon?”

options.stay: “Forget the ramyeon.” You stay exactly where you are
options.two: “Put the water on. I'm having two”

lead_direct.title: {name} and the Chairman's Blind Spot
lead_direct.logline: {name} says in episode two what everyone else is saving for the finale. The chairman's plan did not have a variable like this in it.

lead_careful.title: The Quiet Takeover of {name}
lead_careful.logline: {name} carries twelve episodes without once raising their voice, makes everybody wait, and lands the whole thing at the end.

firstLove_direct.title: {name}, Three Months by Contract
firstLove_direct.logline: It was only supposed to last three months on paper. {name} starts doing things that were never in the contract.

firstLove_careful.title: {name}, the Three Months Unsaid
firstLove_careful.logline: {name} never said it. Which is why somebody still can't throw away the umbrella they were lent.

spark_direct.title: {name} vs. the Office Dating Policy
spark_direct.logline: Two episodes of bad timing, and then {name} just asks. Great for the audience, a nightmare for the writers.

spark_careful.title: One Minute Between {name} and Them
spark_careful.logline: {name} and that person keep reaching the same door a minute apart. Nothing has been said and the whole floor knows.

second_direct.title: {name}, the Episode Eight Confession
second_direct.logline: {name} says it in episode eight and steps back cleanly. Half the audience changes sides that night.

second_careful.title: {name} Is Making Sure They Ate
second_careful.logline: {name} is the one who noticed they'd skipped lunch. It never gets said, and people argue about it until the finale.

rival_direct.title: {name}, the One in the Meeting Room
rival_direct.logline: {name} arrives late, better dressed, and says the thing nobody wanted said. Being right is the annoying part.

rival_careful.title: {name} Already Knew
rival_careful.logline: {name} doesn't fight anyone. It just keeps turning out that {name} was right, and by the time anyone notices it's late.

bestie_direct.title: {name} Is the Mood of This Company
bestie_direct.logline: {name} takes every scene they're in, and half of those scenes were not in the script.

bestie_careful.title: The Company Doesn't Work Without {name}
bestie_careful.logline: {name} drives them home, remembers what was said in episode one, and never makes it about themselves.

wedding.title: A wedding. There's a seat for {name} on the bride's side. You're seeing the groom for the first time today.

options.groom: You don't stop looking at the groom
options.back: You sit at the very back and stay there
options.hands: You go to the bride first and take her hands
options.envelope: You leave your name off the gift envelope

slap.title: A slap, delivered with a handful of kimchi. It didn't land on you.

options.toward: You walk slowly towards the one who was hit
options.wrist2: You catch the wrist that's holding the kimchi
options.towel: You go and get a wet towel first
options.film: You lift your phone. Recording first

photo2.title: An old photo turns up in a drawer. A woman of about twenty, and she looks far too much like {name}.

options.ask2: You take the photo straight to your mother
options.drawer: You put it back and lock the drawer
options.careful: You ask who she is, carefully
options.copy: You photograph it and send it to nobody

hospital2.title: A hospital room. Someone you've never met is calling {name} by name.

options.handonly: You take their hand and ask nothing
options.whoareyou: You ask who they are, straight out
options.chart: You call a nurse and read the chart

will.title: The will is being read. The lawyer says {name}.

options.listen2: You just listen. Your face doesn't move
options.reread: You stand and ask him to read it again in full
options.hold3: You take the hand of the person beside you
options.copy2: You ask the lawyer for a copy

options.stare2: You look at the record for a long time
options.callnow: You ring the director straight away
options.others: You look for the others who were there first
options.take2: You copy the record and put it in your bag

twin.title: Someone messages: they've just seen a person on the street who looks exactly like {name}.

options.keep2: You keep the photo and don't reply
options.gothere: You go straight to where they saw them
options.hush: You decide not to tell the family
options.mimic: You pose as them and send a photo back

dna.title: The paternity result has arrived, still in its envelope. You haven't opened it.

options.openit: You open it where you stand
options.lawyer: You agree to open it with the lawyer present
options.fridge: You put the whole envelope in the fridge

stepmother.title: Your stepmother has tidied your room. Everything except the photo frame.

options.nothing3: You don't bring the frame up
options.whereis: You ask where the frame is, immediately
options.bigger: You buy a bigger frame and hang it higher

amnesia.title: Since the accident they don't recognise {name}.

options.again2: You tell them the same story from the start, every day
options.doctor2: You hear the doctor out to the end first
options.okay: You tell them it's fine not to remember
options.photos: You quietly hang old photos in the room

boardroom.title: The board meeting. Shares come up, and then the name {name}.

options.protect: You state that their shares are not to be touched
options.readall: You read the papers through before saying anything
options.staff: You start with the people still working there
options.delay: You move to push the vote to next week

deathbed.title: At the very end, your mother takes {name} by the hand and tries to say something.

options.listenclose: You put your ear close and listen to the end
options.family2: You call the rest of the family in first
options.dontspeak: You tell her it's alright, she doesn't have to

swap2.title: The hospital calls. Two babies may have been swapped in 1998. One of them is {name}.

options.gohome: You go straight to the parents who raised you
options.records: You demand every record the hospital holds
options.theirs: Your first thought is for the other family
options.alone2: You tell nobody and look into it yourself

crash.title: Wet road. Brakes. And a phone that won't stop ringing.

options.nopick: You don't answer it. You stay where you are
options.umbrella: You hold the umbrella over them and get soaked

secret2.title: There's something your mother hasn't said in twenty years. “I think {name} should hear it from me.”

options.nowhere: You tell her to say it. Now, here
options.quieter: You ask to move somewhere quieter
options.dontneed: You tell her she doesn't have to if it's hard
options.knew: You tell her you already knew

rain.title: Rain. They're standing in it with no umbrella.

options.soaked: You stand next to them and get just as wet
options.tocar: You put the umbrella over them and walk them to the car
options.giveit: You hand them the umbrella and go on
options.throwit: You throw it to them and run

funeral.title: The funeral hall. Your name is on the chief mourner's card.

options.sit2: You take the seat and say nothing
options.greet2: You greet every mourner, one by one
options.beside2: You go and sit next to whoever is crying
options.swapname: You take the card down and put another name on it

reunion2.title: After twenty years, they're standing at the door.

options.silent3: You open the door and say nothing
options.comein: You tell them to come in, before they speak
options.interest: “Twenty years. There's interest on that,” you say

trial.title: A courtroom. You're in the witness box.

options.onlyasked: You answer only what you're asked
options.more2: You say the part nobody asked about
options.dontlook: You don't look their way once
options.gallery: You say something to the public gallery

confront.title: Everyone is in the room. Now you speak.

options.papers: You put the papers on the table and wait
options.neither: You say up front that you're taking nobody's side

forgive.title: “{name}. All you have to do is take my hand.”

options.sitdown: You don't take it. You sit down beside them
options.takeit: You take it, in front of everyone

lead_direct.title: {name} and the Real Name in That House
lead_direct.logline: {name} opens the envelope where they stand. Nobody in that house goes back to how they were.

lead_careful.title: {name} Waited Twenty Years
lead_careful.logline: {name} let twenty years go by without a word. Then, once, with everyone in the room, {name} speaks.

firstLove_direct.title: {name} and a Promise in the Rain
firstLove_direct.logline: {name} can't walk past someone standing in the rain with no umbrella. That once carries a hundred episodes.

firstLove_careful.title: {name} and the Photo in the Drawer
firstLove_careful.logline: {name} put the photo back in the drawer and asked nobody. Which is why nothing was ever finished.

spark_direct.title: {name}, the Second Time
spark_direct.logline: The second time they meet, {name} just asks. One question turns the whole household over.

spark_careful.title: {name} and Them, 1998
spark_careful.logline: {name} and that person passed each other once in 1998. Neither of them knows. Only you do.

second_direct.title: {name} on the Mourner's Card
second_direct.logline: {name}'s name was on the chief mourner's card. {name} sat down, and half the audience changed sides that night.

second_careful.title: {name} Stayed to the End
second_careful.logline: Everyone went home and {name} was still in the corridor. Nobody knew until the final episode.

rival_direct.title: {name}, the Last Line of the Will
rival_direct.logline: {name}'s name was on the last line. {name} stands up and asks for it to be read again.

rival_careful.title: {name}, a Quiet Inheritance
rival_careful.logline: {name} asks for nothing. The shares keep moving {name}'s way regardless.

bestie_direct.title: {name} Is the Noise in This House
bestie_direct.logline: A quiet house gets loud when {name} walks in. Without that noise it would have fallen down already.

bestie_careful.title: {name} Takes Nobody's Side
bestie_careful.logline: {name} won't take sides, which is why {name} is the only one anyone tells the truth to.
